studies.Reference: Habitual intake of lactic acid bacteria and risk reduction of bladder cancer.
studies.Title: Habitual intake of lactic acid bacteria and risk reduction of bladder cancer.
studies.Authors: Ohashi Y, Nakai S, Tsukamoto T, Masumori N, Akaza H, Miyanaga N, Kitamura T, Kawabe K, Kotake T, Kuroda M, Naito S, Koga H, Saito Y, Nomata K, Kitagawa M, Aso Y
studies.Population: cases from 7 hospitals and population-based controls
studies.comparison_type: 3-4 or more times per week versus reference category not stated

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 180 cases (mean age: 67 years, SD 10) were selected from 7 hospitals, and 445 population-based controls matched by gender and age were also selected.
sample_size.location: Abstract, sentence 4; total_n derived from reported group counts 180 + 445 = 625

cases.excerpt: A total of 180 cases (mean age: 67 years, SD 10) were selected from 7 hospitals, and 445 population-based controls matched by gender and age were also selected.

effect_size.excerpt: Those of previous (10-15 years ago) intake of fermented milk products were 0.46 (0.27-0.79) for 1-2 times/week and 0.61 (0.38-0.99) for 3-4 or more times/week, respectively. It was strongly suggested that the habitual intake of lactic acid bacteria reduces the risk of bladder cancer.

confidence_interval.excerpt: The OR of smoking was 1.61 (95% confidence interval: 1.10-2.36). Those of previous (10-15 years ago) intake of fermented milk products were 0.46 (0.27-0.79) for 1-2 times/week and 0.61 (0.38-0.99) for 3-4 or more times/week, respectively.

timing.excerpt: previous (10-15 years ago) intake of fermented milk products

exposure_measurement.excerpt: L. casei, widely taken as fermented milk products in Japan

gender.excerpt: 445 population-based controls matched by gender and age

smoking_status.excerpt: The OR of smoking was 1.61 (95% confidence interval: 1.10-2.36).
